Separate the halves with an irregular horizontal torn-paper edge with visible white fibers. For the cartoon, use 1930s–1950s rubber-hose animation and mid-century illustrated postcard aesthetics: bold, slightly uneven black ink outlines, rounded faces, large oval or pie-cut eyes, curved eyebrows, tiny simplified noses, expressive mouths, subtle cheek blush, flowing sculpted hair, and rounded bare hands. Slightly enlarge heads and simplify bodies while keeping every person recognizable. Preserve hairstyles, outfits, accessories, poses, expressions, camera angle, framing, and background objects. Use flat muted colors, minimal painted shading, dry gouache strokes, colored-pencil texture, aged cream paper, fine print grain, and softly faded edges. Keep the photographic colors recognizable, with warm ochre highlights and muted teal, olive, rust, and brown tones. Render the entire lower background as an illustration too. The result should feel like a charming old printed cartoon postcard, with playful expressions and faithful scene matching. Avoid modern vector polish, glossy 3D rendering, anime, and realistic facial shading. No added text. @RoidBest
